"""
def visualize_tree(tree):
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    tree.build_graph(G)
    pos = nx.spring_layout(G)  # Positioning the nodes
    
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    nx.draw(G, pos, with_labels=True, node_size=3000, node_color='lightblue', font_size=10, font_color='black')
    plt.title("Red-Black Tree Visualization")
    plt.show()
"""

Explanation: - This function generates a visual representation of the Red-Black Tree. - It uses NetworkX to build a graph and matplotlib to render it with labeled nodes and a styled layout.

title: Visualizations
text:
Main Streamlit App


Click to view code

"""
def main():
    st.title('Red-Black Tree Visualization')
    st.write("""
        This is an interactive Red-Black Tree visualization project. 
        You can insert values into the tree and watch how it balances and updates.
    """)

    tree = RedBlackTree()

    value = st.number_input('Enter Value to Insert:', min_value=1, value=0, step=1)

    if st.button('Insert'):
        if value != 0:
            tree.insert(value)
            st.write(f"Value {value} inserted into the tree.")
            visualize_tree(tree)
        else:
            st.write("Please enter a non-zero value.")

    step = st.checkbox('Enable Step-by-Step Insertion', value=False)
    if step:
        st.write("Insert values step by step to visualize tree changes one by one.")

    if st.button('Show In-Order Traversal'):
        in_order = tree.inorder_helper(tree.root)
        st.write(f"In-Order Traversal: {in_order}")
"""

Explanation: - This function creates a complete Streamlit app that lets users interactively build and visualize a Red-Black Tree. - Users can insert values, choose to see the tree change step-by-step, and view an in-order traversal.

title: Conclusion
text:
In this project, we explored the fundamental concepts of Red-Black Trees, which are a type of self-balancing binary search tree that plays a crucial role in various real-world applications, particularly where fast search, insertion, and deletion operations are required. Project Objectives
The primary objective of this project was to develop a comprehensive and interactive visualization tool for Red-Black Trees. This tool was built using Streamlit, NetworkX, and Matplotlib. The goal was not only to implement the Red-Black Tree structure itself but also to create a user-friendly interface that allows users to interact with the tree by inserting nodes and visualizing how the tree adjusts itself after each operation.
By integrating explanations directly into the code, we aimed to make the algorithm more accessible to a broader audience, including those who might find tree rotations and balancing operations challenging to understand. This project aimed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical visualization, enabling users to grasp the complexities of Red-Black Trees by visually observing their dynamics in real-time.


Challenges and Future Improvements
While the project successfully demonstrates how Red-Black Trees function and how their operations are visualized, there are several areas for future improvement: 1. Deletion Visualization: Although the current project focuses on insertions and rotations, adding deletion functionality to the visualization would further enrich the understanding of Red-Black Trees. 2. Performance Benchmarks: The current app allows for visualizing the tree’s structure, but incorporating performance benchmarks that compare the efficiency of Red-Black Trees to other data structures (like AVL Trees or simple Binary Search Trees) would provide additional insights into their performance. 3. Advanced User Interaction: Enhancing the user interface to allow users to manipulate the tree, such as by dragging nodes or manually adjusting the tree’s structure, could provide a more interactive experience.


Final Thoughts
Overall, this project serves as an excellent introduction to Red-Black Trees and provides a comprehensive visualization tool that aids in understanding how these self-balancing trees maintain their structure. By combining theoretical explanations with interactive visualizations, the project bridges the gap between understanding Red-Black Trees as abstract concepts and applying them in practical scenarios.
The ability to visually track how a Red-Black Tree balances itself with every insertion makes this project a valuable educational resource for anyone learning about data structures. In the future, expanding this project to include deletion, performance comparisons, and enhanced interactivity could further enrich the learning experience for users.
In conclusion, this project not only demonstrates the mechanics of Red-Black Trees but also highlights the power of visualizing complex algorithms and their real-world applications in a way that makes them more accessible to a broad audience.

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation

"""
class RedBlackTree:
    def __init__(self):
        self.TNULL = RedBlackNode(0)  # Sentinel node (used for leaves)
        self.TNULL.color = 'black'    # The sentinel node is always black
        self.root = self.TNULL         # Root is initially set to TNULL
"""

Explanation: - The RedBlackTree class is the main structure that implements the Red-Black Tree. - It includes a sentinel node, TNULL, which is used for all leaf nodes in the tree. This node is always colored black. - The root is initialized as TNULL, meaning that the tree is empty when first created.

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
Click to view code

"""
    def rotate_left(self, x):
        y = x.right
        x.right = y.left
        if y.left != self.TNULL:
            y.left.parent = x
        y.parent = x.parent
        if x.parent == None:
            self.root = y
        elif x == x.parent.left:
            x.parent.left = y
        else:
            x.parent.right = y
        y.left = x
        x.parent = y
"""

Explanation: - This method performs a left rotation on a given node x. - After the rotation, the original node x becomes the left child of its right child y, and y becomes the parent of x.

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation

"""
    def fix_insert(self, k):
        while k.parent.color == 'red':
            if k.parent == k.parent.parent.left:
                u = k.parent.parent.right
                if u.color == 'red':
                    u.color = 'black'
                    k.parent.color = 'black'
                    k.parent.parent.color = 'red'
                    k = k.parent.parent
                else:
                    if k == k.parent.right:
                        k = k.parent
                        self.rotate_left(k)
                    k.parent.color = 'black'
                    k.parent.parent.color = 'red'
                    self.rotate_right(k.parent.parent)
            else:
                u = k.parent.parent.left
                if u.color == 'red':
                    u.color = 'black'
                    k.parent.color = 'black'
                    k.parent.parent.color = 'red'
                    k = k.parent.parent
                else:
                    if k == k.parent.left:
                        k = k.parent
                        self.rotate_right(k)
                    k.parent.color = 'black'
                    k.parent.parent.color = 'red'
                    self.rotate_left(k.parent.parent)
            if k == self.root:
                break
        self.root.color = 'black'
"""

Explanation: - Fixes violations of Red-Black Tree properties after an insertion by performing color changes and rotations.

title: Red-Black Tree Implementation
text:
Click to view code

"""
    def insert(self, key):
        node = RedBlackNode(key)
        node.parent = None
        node.key = key
        node.left = self.TNULL
        node.right = self.TNULL
        node.color = 'red'

        y = None
        x = self.root

        while x != self.TNULL:
            y = x
            if node.key < x.key:
                x = x.left
            else:
                x = x.right

        node.parent = y
        if y == None:
            self.root = node
        elif node.key < y.key:
            y.left = node
        else:
            y.right = node

        if node.parent == None:
            node.color = 'black'
            return

        if node.parent.parent == None:
            return

        self.fix_insert(node)
"""

Explanation: - This function inserts a new node in the tree and then fixes any Red-Black Tree violations caused by the insertion.

title: About
text:
Red-Black Tree Visuals
The visualization is built using NetworkX and Matplotlib, with the following features: 1. Tree Structure: The tree is displayed with nodes and edges. Each node is labeled with its key, and the edges represent the parent-child relationships. 2. Node Colors: Nodes are colored based on their Red-Black Tree color (red or black). 3. Rotations and Balancing: As values are inserted, the visualization dynamically updates the tree to reflect any rotations or color changes needed to maintain balance.
